questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All leaves are green.

II. Some leaves are hard.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some hard are green.

II. All green are leaves.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d6a05e22751877b96202ca4dd0e5f1734b9ed3f619d10a70fef3455b1f0c9f3.png] 

I. Some hard are green. → True (As, All leaves are green and some leaves are hard → Some hard are green)

II. All green are leaves. → False (It can be possible but it is not definite)

Hence, only conclusion (I) follows.

questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a piece of work in 45, 15 and 5 days respectively. In how may days all three together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given**

P, Q and R can complete a piece of work in 45,15 and 5 days respectively.

**Calculation**

Let total work be 45 units (LCM of 45, 15 and 5).

Hence, efficiency of P = 45/45 = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of Q = 45/15 = 3 units/day

Efficiency of R = 45/5 = 9 units/day

Now, combined efficiency of all three = 1 + 3 + 9 = 13 units

∴ Time taken to complete same work by all three = Total work/Total efficiency = 45/13 days.

questions.question: In India, inflation is measured on the basis of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Consumer price index.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inflation** refers to the rise in the average price level of goods and services leading to a decline in the value of money within a particular economy.
 
• The wholesale price index and the consumer price index are the two main indicators of inflation in India.
 
• The wholesale price index is considered as the primary inflation measure in India.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India had adopted the **consumer price index as its key measure of inflation in India** since 2014.
 
• **The consumer price index** is the measure of the average change over time in the prices of consumer goods and services purchased by households.
 
 
• The percentage change in the consumer price index over a period of time gives the amount of inflation over that specific period.
 
• Consumer Price Index in India is published by the Central Statistical Organization (CSO).
 
• It is published monthly in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Wholesale Price Index** measures the average change in the prices of commodities for bulk sale at the level of the early stage of transactions.

 
 
• Countries like the Philippines use wholesale price index changes as a central measure of inflation.
 
• The wholesale price index is published by the office of economic adviser, ministry of commerce and industry.
 
 
 
• **The Producer Price Index **is the measure of the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers of goods and services.

questions.question: The workforce population includes people aged from ______ years to ______ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15, 59.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The workforce population includes people aged from **15 years to 59 years.**
 
• The workforce population indicates the share of the **working-age population** in the total population.
 
• The working-age population is the total population in a particular area that is considered able and likely to work based on the number of people in a predetermined age range.
 
• The working-age population gives an estimate of the total number of potential workers within an economy.
 
• The age limits of the working-age population can vary from country to country.
 
• There were around **521 million workers in India**, the second largest after China based on the world factbook data.

questions.question: In which type of economy there is neither exports nor imports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Closed.**__

 
• An economy having no economic relationship with other countries is called a **closed economy.**

 
 
• **There is neither exports nor imports in a closed economy.**
 
• Goods are produced and consumed by the same households within a closed economy.
 
• The hunter-gatherer societies are the best examples of a closed economy.
 
• A closed economy should be **entirely self-sufficient.**
 
• There are no nations that have economies that are completely closed in reality.
 
 
 
• An economy that has economic relations with other countries of the world is called an **open economy.**
 
 
• There should be exports and imports in an open economy.
 
• Exporting is the process of selling goods or services to a foreign country.
 
• Importing is the process of buying goods or services from a foreign country.
 
 
 
• The economy that left to the free market, and part of it is managed by the government called a **mixed economy.**
 
 
• Both privately owned businesses and governments play important roles in a mixed economy.
 
 
 
• The interconnected worldwide economic activities that take place between multiple countries is called a **global economy.**

questions.question: Which price is declared by the government every year before the sowing season to provide incentives to the farmers for raising the production of their crops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Minimum Support Price**__.

The minimum support price is the price is declared by the government to **insure agricultural producers against any sharp fall in farm prices**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• It is announced by the government of India every year **before the sowing season **and provides incentives to the farmers for raising the production of their crops.
 
• The crops were selected based on the recommendations of the **commission for agricultural costs and Prices(CACP).**
 
• If the market price for the commodity falls below the minimum support price due to the issues in the market, government agencies purchase the entire quantity at the announced minimum price.
 
• In India, there are **twenty-two crops** covered under Minimum Support Price.
 
• The 22 mandated crops under MSP consist of **14 Kharif crops, 6 rabi crops, and two other commercial crops**.
 
• Some important minimum support price crops in India are:
 
 
• Paddy, wheat, barley, jowar, bajra, maize, and ragi.
 
• Gram, arhar/tur, moong, urad and lentil.
 
• Groundnut, mustard, sunflower seed, sesamum, and safflower seed.

questions.question: What is an association of workers for the purpose of maintaining or improving the conditions of their employment called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Trade Union.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Trade Union is an association of workers to maintain or improve the conditions of their employment.

 
 
• Trade union acts as a bargaining agent and legal representative for employees in all matters of law or the administration of a collective agreement.
 
• Ministry of labour and employment is the regulatory authority of trade unions in India.
 
• Bharatiya mazdoor Sangh is considered as the largest trade union of India.
 
 
 
• Bombay mill hands association founded by N.M. Lokhande in 1890 was the first organised labour union in India.
 
• Madras labour union founded by B.P. Wadia in 1918 is considered as the first clearly registered trade-union in India.

questions.question: Chahamanas who ruled over the region around Delhi and Ajmer were later known as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chauhans.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Chahamanas who ruled over the region around Delhi and Ajmer were later known as Chauhans.
 
• The capital of Chahamanas was in **Shakambhari.**
 
• Chahamanas dynasty ruled the Indian subcontinent between** the 6th to 12th centuries.**
 
• They ruled over the present-day **Rajasthan** and its neighboring areas.
 
• They moved the kingdom's capital to Ajayameru (modern **Ajmer**) in the 12th century.
 
• The capital was moved to Ajmer by the ruler **Ajayaraja II.**
 
• The dynasty's Chahamanas were disestablished in **1192 CE.**

 
 

 Chalukyas dynasty
 
 
 
• The rise of the **Chalukyas **marks an important milestone in the history of South India and a golden age in the history of Karnataka.
 
• The political atmosphere in South India shifted from smaller kingdoms to large empires with the rise of **Badami Chalukyas.**
 
• Chalukyas of Badami were the successors of the Vakatakas in western Deccan.
 
• They established their capital at Vatapi, modern Badami in the Bijapur district. Later they branched off into several independent ruling houses, but the main branch continued to rule at Vatapi. 
 
 
 
 

 Cholas
 
 
 
• One of the longest-ruling dynasties in south India.
 
• Ruled between 300 CE and 1279 CE.
 
• One of the three crowned kings of Tamilakam.
 
• Chola dynasty was founded by Vijayalaya.
 
• Rajendra Chola III was the last Chola ruler.
 
 
 
 

 Chandelas
 
 
 
• Ruled between the 9th and the 13th centuries.
 
• Dynasty in Central India.
 
• The original capital was in Khajuraho.
 
• Manuka was the first king of Chandelas.
